title: Understanding the Implications of the Energy Transition on African Economies: Economy and Jobs
description: Assessment of how large-scale renewable energy deployment affects employment, GDP, and structural economic shifts across African economies during the clean energy transition.
methodology: Input-output and jobs multiplier analysis across energy value chains; scenario modelling of RE share targets.
assumptions: Grid expansion keeps pace with generation investment
Local content policies affect domestic job creation
Fossil fuel sectors face gradual demand decline
limitations: Aggregate Africa-wide patterns mask country heterogeneity
Job quality and informal sector dynamics not fully captured

sources.title: UNFCCC KCI — Energy transition Africa economy and jobs

nodes.label: Shift from diesel/gensets & biomass to grid/solar

outcomes.description: Direct and indirect jobs in solar/wind installation, grid works, and O&M
Energy sector investment stimulates GDP through construction and supply chains
Expanded generation improves electricity access rates
Displacement of fossil generation reduces energy-sector emissions
Transition away from fossil fuel operations reduces legacy sector employment
Distributed solar and mini-grids create local installation jobs with higher female participation than fossil sectors in several African case studies
Off-grid renewables improve electricity access for rural households previously excluded from the central grid

trade_offs.negative_effect: Workforce displacement in fossil fuel sectors without reskilling
